title: Inflation! a co-op incremental RPG
author: KurusuDesu
selftext:
Hello! I just want to share this little game I've been building over the past few months. It's a simple roguelite adventure in which a map is created by a seed. Even though you win a lot of levels per match, that's the incremental part. The way you build your character, unlock a lot of things, and plan your path every run is the main key point.

It's not that easy to just go brainless and follow one route otherwise, you will get crushed at some point or against some bosses that have more or less affinity with your build.

You have a limited amount of tries. After that, you restart with the map and the planes from the bosses you killed. Overall, it's a little adventure of about 3–4 hours.

I had my friends test it for a bit. The hard part was the balance, which is not perfect, but I think it's polished enough to get some raw feedback. It has a full demo on [itch.io](http://itch.io/), but I had some problems with the multiplayer. I'm currently working on the full version with cloud services in Unity, which I plan to release on the Play Store! I also plan to release the pc version on my Discord channel.

Anyways, I hope you try it! It might look simple in the beginning, but it has a lot of depth once you start your second run. Each run is about 20 minutes.

If you want to try it out, the link is:  
[https://teapartygamestudio.itch.io/inflation-coop-rpg](https://teapartygamestudio.itch.io/inflation-coop-rpg)

It also really shines when playing with friends. I had a lot of fun testing it with up to 5 players, with everyone going for what we thought was the best path to defeat the final boss. The mini PvP between us also made for some good laughs! I forgot add the variaty of biomes and enemys that I had a lot of fun inventing the names that the little cherry for you to see while playing , the names also have some clues about the type of enemies they are! If you made it this far, thanks!

AI disclosure:  
Code: Mostly AI, reviewed by myself.  
Art: All models were made in Blender.

**About my AI workflow:**  
A big part of my workflow is having a complete and detailed GDD about the idea I want to build and always keeping the scope under control. Most of my first iterations involved having the details from beginning to end about what I wanted to build.  
After that, I store the overall path and the requirements for each phase of development. This helps me avoid AI hallucinations by using Markdown and Obsidian to keep a record of which phase I was currently in and which bugs I was working on.

Another thing I needed the most was feedback from my friends. AI tends to have a really bad sense of balance, so having a tool to collect data from my playthroughs and my friends' playthroughs was really useful.
